title: Conormal sheaf of a formally unramified morphism
statement: Let $h:Z\to X$ be a formally unramified morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism]. Choose a universal first order thickening $Z\subset Z'$ of $Z$ over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening], with closed immersion $i:Z\to Z'$; it exists and is unique up to a unique isomorphism over $X$ compatible with $i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening-exists]. Let $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_{Z'}$ be the ideal sheaf of $i$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], so $\mathcal I^2=0$. The *conormal sheaf of $Z$ over $X$* is the $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal C_{Z/X}:=i^*(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2)=i^*\mathcal I$ [def-pc-module-pullback], the conormal sheaf of the closed immersion $i$; via the unique isomorphism of universal thickenings it does not depend on the choice up to unique isomorphism.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Definition 04F4 (definition-universal-thickening) (2); the conormal sheaf of a closed immersion is Morphisms, Definition 01R2 (morphisms-definition-conormal-sheaf)

proof.text: (Choice of thickening.) By [lem-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening-exists], the formally unramified morphism $h:Z\to X$ admits a universal first order thickening $i:Z\to Z'$ over $X$. The same lemma gives the unique isomorphism over $X$, compatible with $i$, between any two such choices.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening) and Section Tag 04F2, opening uniqueness discussion

proof.text: (The ideal sheaf.) For the chosen closed immersion $i:Z\to Z'$, let $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_{Z'}\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$, the ideal sheaf of the immersion [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Because $Z\subset Z'$ is first order, the defining ideal satisfies $\mathcal I^2=0$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. Thus $\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is canonically $\mathcal I$ as an $\mathcal O_{Z'}$-module.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Definition Tag 04F4 (definition-universal-thickening), item (2), together with Definition Tag 04EX (definition-thickening), item (2), and Morphisms Definition Tag 01R2

proof.text: (The conormal module.) Pull the quotient module $\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ back along $i$ using the module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. This produces an $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal C_{Z/X}:=i^*(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2)=i^*\mathcal I$. It is precisely the conormal sheaf of the closed immersion $i$, so the displayed object has the claimed module structure and notation.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Definition Tag 04F4 item (2), invoking Morphisms Definition Tag 01R2 (morphisms-definition-conormal-sheaf); module pullback is Sheaves Tag 0095

proof.text: (Independence of the choice.) If $(Z'_1,i_1)$ and $(Z'_2,i_2)$ are two universal thickenings, the unique compatible isomorphism $\varphi:Z'_1\xrightarrow{\sim}Z'_2$ identifies their ideal sheaves and, after applying the pullback along the common closed subscheme $Z$, identifies $i_1^*(\mathcal I_1/\mathcal I_1^2)$ with $i_2^*(\mathcal I_2/\mathcal I_2^2)$. The uniqueness clause makes this identification independent of any choices and functorial, so $\mathcal C_{Z/X}$ is defined up to the unique canonical isomorphism asserted in the statement.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Section Tag 04F2 and Definition Tag 04F4 item (2), using the unique isomorphism of universal thickenings from Lemma Tag 04F3
